title: Constancy after reindexing the restriction
statement: Let $n\in\mathbb{N}$, let $f:\{−1,1\}^n\to\{−1,1\}$ be a Boolean function, let $P\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}$, fix an assignment $z$ on $P$, and let $c\in\{−1,1\}$. If the reindexed restriction of $f$ is constantly $c$ on the sign cube whose dimension is the number of coordinates outside $P$, then the restriction itself is constantly $c$ on assignments to those free coordinates.
hypotheses_covered: Reindexed restriction is constant with value c
